quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Compliment With a Catch] In front of the whole team, the director praises Farid's report as 'thorough and well-researched,' then adds, almost as an afterthought while already turning to the next agenda item, that it might have been 'even stronger with a tighter executive summary.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about how the director's feedback was delivered?
options: The criticism was the main focus of the entire meeting.
The criticism was minimized to avoid overshadowing the public praise.
The praise was withdrawn immediately after being given.
No criticism was given at any point.
quests.correctAnswer: The criticism was minimized to avoid overshadowing the public praise.
quests.hint: Think about what saying something 'almost as an afterthought,' while already moving to the next topic, suggests about how much weight it was meant to carry.
quests.explanation: Adding the critique almost as an afterthought while moving on suggests the director wanted to note it without letting it overshadow the public praise.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Silence at the Dinner Table] Every other Sunday dinner for the past year, Aunt Rosa has asked pointed questions about when her niece plans to settle down, but tonight, after the niece mentions a new job opportunity abroad, Aunt Rosa says nothing on the subject at all and instead asks about the flight schedule.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Aunt Rosa's shift in questions?
options: She is more focused on settling down than ever before.
She has forgotten her usual questions entirely.
She did not hear the news about the job opportunity.
She may be adjusting her expectations based on the new information.
quests.correctAnswer: She may be adjusting her expectations based on the new information.
quests.hint: Think about what dropping a recurring topic, right after hearing specific news, and pivoting to a related practical question suggests.
quests.explanation: Dropping her usual questions right after hearing about the job opportunity, and instead asking about flights, suggests Aunt Rosa may be adjusting her focus based on this new direction.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Discount That Isn't Quite What It Seems] The 'Buy One, Get One 50% Off' sign hangs above the display, but a closer look at the price tags shows the items were marked up by roughly the amount of the advertised discount just three days before the promotion began, according to the store's own price-history sticker.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the actual savings from this promotion?
options: The prices were lowered before the promotion, not raised.
They may be smaller than the advertised discount suggests.
They are exactly as advertised, with no hidden adjustments.
The promotion offers savings greater than what is advertised.
quests.correctAnswer: They may be smaller than the advertised discount suggests.
quests.hint: Think about what raising prices just before a discount, by roughly the same amount, does to the real value of that discount.
quests.explanation: Marking up prices just before applying an equivalent discount suggests the real savings to customers may be smaller than the advertised percentage implies.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Study Cited Without Its Caveats] The supplement's packaging cites 'a university study' showing benefits for joint health, but the original study, available online, describes its own sample size as 'too small for broad conclusions' and specifically recommends further research before any claims are made to consumers.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how the packaging represents the study?
options: It presents the findings more confidently than the researchers themselves did.
The original study encouraged exactly this kind of marketing claim.
It accurately reflects every caveat mentioned in the original study.
It understates the strength of the original study's conclusions.
quests.correctAnswer: It presents the findings more confidently than the researchers themselves did.
quests.hint: Compare the confident marketing claim with the researchers' own cautious language about their small sample size.
quests.explanation: Citing the study without its stated caveats about small sample size suggests the packaging presents the findings with more confidence than the original researchers intended.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Feature Removed Without Fanfare] The app's release notes for the latest update list several new features in detail but make no mention of the offline mode that previously allowed users to access saved content without an internet connection, a feature that stops working entirely after the update installs.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the removal of the offline mode?
options: Users were given advance notice before the feature was removed.
The removal was prominently announced as a major update.
The company may have preferred not to draw attention to this change.
The offline mode was replaced with an improved offline feature.
quests.correctAnswer: The company may have preferred not to draw attention to this change.
quests.hint: Think about why a company would detail new features but stay silent about something being taken away.
quests.explanation: Detailing new features while staying silent about a removed one suggests the company may have preferred this particular change go unnoticed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [An Actor's Careful Answer] When asked directly in an interview whether he will return for the next film in the series, the actor laughs, says 'you'll have to ask the studio that one,' and quickly pivots to discussing his character's arc in the current film in unusually specific detail.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the actor's response?
options: He has no opinion or knowledge about his future involvement.
He confirmed clearly that he will not return.
He is likely avoiding a direct answer rather than genuinely not knowing.
He confirmed clearly that he will return.
quests.correctAnswer: He is likely avoiding a direct answer rather than genuinely not knowing.
quests.hint: Think about what deflecting the direct question, while speaking in detail about something else, suggests about what he might actually know.
quests.explanation: Deflecting the direct question while speaking in unusual detail about his character suggests the actor may know more than he is willing to say outright.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Guide Who Watches the Weather] Twenty minutes before departure, the mountain guide steps away from the group twice to check something on his phone, then quietly swaps the day's planned summit route for a shorter, lower trail, telling the group only that conditions 'looked better this way.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the reason for the guide's route change?
options: He was checking messages unrelated to the hike.
He likely saw information, such as a weather update, that concerned him.
He made the change for no particular reason at all.
The original route was always going to be used regardless.
quests.correctAnswer: He likely saw information, such as a weather update, that concerned him.
quests.hint: Think about what checking his phone twice, right before changing to a safer, shorter route, suggests about what he saw.
quests.explanation: Checking his phone repeatedly right before switching to a shorter, lower route suggests the guide likely saw information, such as a weather update, that prompted the safer choice.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Raise That Comes with a Warning] Along with news of her raise, Talia's manager mentions, almost in passing, that the department's budget for next year is still being finalized and that 'nothing is guaranteed until it's guaranteed,' a phrase Talia has never heard him use before.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the manager's underlying message?
options: He may want to prepare her for the possibility of future budget cuts.
He is completely certain next year's budget will increase.
The comment has no connection to the department's finances.
He wants to withdraw the raise immediately.
quests.correctAnswer: He may want to prepare her for the possibility of future budget cuts.
quests.hint: Think about why the manager would pair good news with an unusual, cautious phrase about guarantees.
quests.explanation: Pairing the raise with an unusual, cautious comment about the budget not being guaranteed suggests the manager may be preparing Talia for possible uncertainty ahead.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Silent Classroom After the Announcement] When the principal announces over the intercom that the beloved art teacher, Ms. Reyes, will not be returning next year 'due to a restructuring of elective offerings,' the usually noisy classroom falls completely silent, and several students exchange glances rather than returning to their work.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the students' reaction to the announcement?
options: They are relieved that Ms. Reyes will not be returning.
They are likely surprised or upset by the news.
They already knew about this change well in advance.
They are completely indifferent to the announcement.
quests.correctAnswer: They are likely surprised or upset by the news.
quests.hint: Think about what sudden silence and exchanged glances, from a normally noisy classroom, suggest about their emotional reaction.
quests.explanation: A normally noisy classroom falling silent, with students exchanging glances instead of working, suggests the news caught them off guard and affected them emotionally.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Recipe That Leaves Something Out] The celebrity chef's cookbook lists exact measurements for every ingredient except one, the 'secret spice blend,' which is described only as 'a pinch of something special,' even though every other recipe in the book specifies exact amounts down to the quarter-teaspoon.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the vague description of the spice blend?
options: It may be intentionally left unclear to protect a proprietary recipe.
The chef does not actually know what is in the blend.
It reflects the chef's general writing style throughout the book.
It was simply an oversight the editor failed to catch.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be intentionally left unclear to protect a proprietary recipe.
quests.hint: Think about why every other ingredient is precisely measured, except this one specific item.
quests.explanation: Precise measurements throughout the book, except for one deliberately vague ingredient, suggest the vagueness is likely intentional, possibly to protect a proprietary blend.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Petition That Changes Its Ask] The neighborhood petition originally calls for a full ban on overnight street parking, but after several meetings with residents who rely on street parking, the final version submitted to the city instead requests permits and designated time limits, a noticeably softer request than the first draft.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the reason for the change between drafts?
options: Feedback from affected residents likely shaped a more moderate proposal.
The final version was identical to the original draft.
No resident feedback was considered in the final version.
The organizers decided to make the request more restrictive.
quests.correctAnswer: Feedback from affected residents likely shaped a more moderate proposal.
quests.hint: Think about what happened between the original draft and the final version, and why the request became less strict.
quests.explanation: A shift from a full ban to permits and time limits, occurring after meetings with affected residents, suggests their feedback led to a more moderate, compromise proposal.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Rating System That Rarely Shows Low Scores] The delivery app allows customers to rate drivers from one to five stars, but a former employee mentions in an interview that ratings below three stars trigger an automatic review process that frequently results in the rating being removed 'for quality control purposes.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the app's average displayed ratings?
options: They accurately reflect every single rating submitted by customers.
They are lower than the ratings customers actually submit.
They may appear higher than they would if every rating were counted.
The review process has no effect on the ratings customers see.
quests.correctAnswer: They may appear higher than they would if every rating were counted.
quests.hint: Think about what removing many low ratings, but presumably not removing high ones, would do to the overall average shown to the public.
quests.explanation: A process that frequently removes low ratings, without removing high ones, would likely make the displayed average appear higher than the full set of actual ratings.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Wellness Program With Fine Print] The company's new wellness program advertises a 'generous' annual reimbursement for gym memberships, but employees who read the full policy discover the reimbursement is capped at an amount that covers less than half the cost of the gym the company itself recommends in the same email.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the term 'generous' as used in this email?
options: It accurately describes the actual value of the reimbursement.
It refers to a completely different benefit than the gym reimbursement.
It understates how much the reimbursement actually covers.
It may overstate how much the reimbursement actually covers.
quests.correctAnswer: It may overstate how much the reimbursement actually covers.
quests.hint: Compare the word 'generous' with the actual coverage amount described later in the policy.
quests.explanation: Calling the reimbursement 'generous' while it covers less than half the recommended gym's cost suggests the description overstates the benefit's real value.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Layover That Grows Longer] Ravi's booking confirmation initially listed a ninety-minute layover, but by the time he checks in online three weeks later, the same itinerary shows a four-hour layover instead, with no explanation offered and no option to select a different connecting flight.
quests.question: What can be inferred about this change to Ravi's itinerary?
options: The airline likely adjusted its schedule after his original booking.
Ravi personally requested the longer layover.
The original ninety-minute layover was never actually booked.
The airline offered him several alternative flight options.
quests.correctAnswer: The airline likely adjusted its schedule after his original booking.
quests.hint: Think about what changing without any explanation, three weeks after booking, suggests about who made this adjustment.
quests.explanation: A change appearing weeks after booking, without explanation or alternative options, suggests the airline adjusted its own schedule rather than Ravi requesting the change.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Team Meeting Rescheduled Three Times] The quarterly all-hands meeting, which typically proceeds without issue, gets rescheduled three separate times in as many weeks, each time by the executive team with only a brief note citing 'scheduling conflicts,' while rumors about a possible reorganization circulate quietly among staff.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the reason behind the repeated rescheduling?
options: The meeting has been permanently cancelled.
It is definitely unrelated to any internal discussions.
It may be connected to unresolved internal discussions, possibly related to the rumored reorganization.
Staff have stopped speculating about the reason entirely.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be connected to unresolved internal discussions, possibly related to the rumored reorganization.
quests.hint: Think about what repeated last-minute rescheduling, alongside circulating rumors, suggests about what might be happening behind the scenes.
quests.explanation: Three rescheduled meetings alongside circulating reorganization rumors suggest the delays may be connected to unresolved internal decisions rather than simple scheduling issues.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Silence About the Photo] Whenever visitors ask about the framed photo of a young man on the mantel, Grandma changes the subject smoothly and offers more tea, a pattern so consistent that her grandchildren have learned not to ask, even though none of them actually know who is in the photo.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the photo's significance to Grandma?
options: She enjoys discussing the photo whenever it comes up.
She has simply forgotten who is in the photo.
It likely holds emotional weight that she prefers not to discuss.
It holds no particular meaning to her at all.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely holds emotional weight that she prefers not to discuss.
quests.hint: Think about what consistently redirecting the conversation, rather than simply answering, suggests about her feelings toward the subject.
quests.explanation: Consistently changing the subject rather than answering suggests the photo likely carries emotional weight that Grandma prefers to keep private.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Show Renewed, Then Quietly Shelved] The network publicly announces the drama's renewal for a fourth season with a press release and social media campaign, but six months later, with no new statement issued, cast members begin posting about new, unrelated projects, and the show's official social accounts go silent.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the status of the renewed season?
options: It may have been delayed or quietly reconsidered despite the earlier announcement.
The show was cancelled through an official statement.
Production is proceeding exactly as originally announced.
The cast is taking a planned break before filming begins.
quests.correctAnswer: It may have been delayed or quietly reconsidered despite the earlier announcement.
quests.hint: Think about what cast members moving to other projects, combined with total silence from the show's accounts, suggests about the renewal's actual status.
quests.explanation: Cast members joining unrelated projects and the show's accounts going silent, despite an earlier renewal announcement, suggest the season may have been delayed or reconsidered without a formal statement.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Loyalty Program That Changes the Math] The retailer's loyalty program once let members redeem 500 points for a $10 reward, but the terms quietly change to require 750 points for the same reward, announced only through a small update buried in an email whose subject line reads 'Exciting News About Your Rewards!'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the framing of this email's subject line?
options: It refers to an unrelated improvement to the program.
It accurately reflects that the change benefits members.
It clearly states that rewards are becoming harder to earn.
It presents the change more positively than the actual content supports.
quests.correctAnswer: It presents the change more positively than the actual content supports.
quests.hint: Compare the enthusiastic subject line with what actually changed for members trying to redeem points.
quests.explanation: An upbeat subject line announcing a change that actually makes rewards harder to earn suggests the framing presents the update more positively than its real impact on members.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Project Handed Off Quietly] Without any formal announcement, the flagship project Mr. Iyer had led for two years is reassigned to a colleague, mentioned to him only briefly in a one-on-one where his manager describes it as an opportunity for him to 'focus on higher-priority initiatives.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about how this reassignment was likely perceived?
options: The project was cancelled entirely rather than reassigned.
It may have been a demotion in responsibility framed in more positive language.
Mr. Iyer requested the reassignment himself in writing.
It was clearly presented and celebrated as a well-earned promotion.
quests.correctAnswer: It may have been a demotion in responsibility framed in more positive language.
quests.hint: Think about what losing a flagship project you led for two years, softened by vague positive language, might actually represent.
quests.explanation: Losing a long-led flagship project, softened with language about 'higher-priority initiatives,' suggests this reassignment may function as a demotion presented in more favorable terms.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Support Group That Grows Without Advertising] The grief support group meets in a small room at the community center, never advertised beyond a single flyer posted eighteen months ago, yet attendance has grown from four people to over twenty, almost entirely through word of mouth among past and current members.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the value members find in this group?
options: The group's growth is due mainly to paid advertising.
Members likely find it meaningful enough to recommend it personally to others.
Attendance has stayed the same since it started.
Members have generally found the group unhelpful.
quests.correctAnswer: Members likely find it meaningful enough to recommend it personally to others.
quests.hint: Think about what growing significantly through word of mouth alone, without advertising, suggests about what members think of the group.
quests.explanation: Growing from four to over twenty members almost entirely through word of mouth suggests current members find real value in the group and are motivated to recommend it to others.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Clinic's Careful Scheduling] The specialist's office always books Mrs. Ferro's appointments as the last of the day, a pattern she does not notice until a new receptionist mentions offhand that 'the doctor likes to have extra time for your visits, just in case there's a lot to go over.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the nature of Mrs. Ferro's typical appointments?
options: They are scheduled last purely by random chance.
The doctor prefers to end the day early because of her visits.
They are shorter than the average patient's appointments.
They likely tend to require more time or discussion than a standard visit.
quests.correctAnswer: They likely tend to require more time or discussion than a standard visit.
quests.hint: Think about why a doctor would deliberately want extra unscheduled time specifically for one patient's visits.
quests.explanation: Deliberately reserving extra time by scheduling her last suggests Mrs. Ferro's appointments typically involve more discussion or complexity than a standard visit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Cruise Itinerary With a Footnote] The cruise brochure prominently advertises a stop at a popular island destination, but a small footnote on the final page notes that port calls are 'subject to change based on operational factors,' a disclaimer that past passengers on travel forums say has affected their itinerary more often than the brochure's photos would suggest.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how reliable the advertised itinerary actually is?
options: The footnote is purely a legal formality with no real impact.
It is completely guaranteed and has never changed for any passenger.
It may be less certain than the prominent photos and descriptions suggest.
Past passengers have never experienced any itinerary changes.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be less certain than the prominent photos and descriptions suggest.
quests.hint: Think about what past passengers' comments about the footnote's real-world impact suggest about the gap between marketing and reality.
quests.explanation: Past passengers reporting that the disclaimer affects itineraries more than advertised, despite the prominent island photos, suggests the advertised schedule is less certain than it initially appears.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Syllabus That Changed Overnight] On the first day of class, the syllabus lists three exams worth 20 percent each, but by the end of the week, an updated version posted online shows a single final exam worth 60 percent instead, with no announcement made about the change during class.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how students learned of this change?
options: Every student was individually emailed about the update.
Many students may not have noticed the change unless they checked the syllabus again themselves.
The professor announced the change clearly during class.
The grading structure stayed exactly the same as the first version.
quests.correctAnswer: Many students may not have noticed the change unless they checked the syllabus again themselves.
quests.hint: Think about what posting a change online, without any in-class announcement, suggests about how likely students were to notice it.
quests.explanation: Updating the syllabus online without announcing it in class suggests many students may have missed the change unless they happened to check the document again.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Loading Screen That Lingers] The app's loading screen, which used to disappear within two seconds, now displays for closer to eight seconds after the latest update, though the release notes describe the update as focused entirely on 'performance improvements.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the update's actual effect on performance?
options: It had no measurable effect on loading time at all.
It made the app load noticeably faster than before.
The loading screen's speed remained completely unchanged.
It may not have improved performance in every way the release notes suggest.
quests.correctAnswer: It may not have improved performance in every way the release notes suggest.
quests.hint: Compare the described purpose of the update with what actually happened to the loading time.
quests.explanation: A loading screen that now takes four times as long, despite an update billed as a 'performance improvement,' suggests the update may not have improved performance as thoroughly as described.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Dish Renamed on the Menu] The 'Grandma's Original Meatballs' disappear from the menu one week and reappear the next simply as 'House Meatballs,' with the recipe, according to a server who has worked there for years, quietly changed to use a cheaper cut of meat in between.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the reason for the name change?
options: The restaurant renamed the dish purely for legal reasons unrelated to ingredients.
It may reflect a shift away from the original recipe the name once described.
The dish was renamed to use a more expensive cut of meat.
It reflects no change in the recipe or ingredients at all.
quests.correctAnswer: It may reflect a shift away from the original recipe the name once described.
quests.hint: Think about why a name tied to a specific origin story would be dropped right around the same time the recipe itself changed.
quests.explanation: Dropping the name tied to a specific origin, right as the recipe quietly changes to a cheaper cut, suggests the rename may reflect a departure from what the original name promised.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Family Text Thread Gone Quiet] The family group chat, usually buzzing with daily messages, has had only two messages in the past week, both from the youngest cousin asking simple questions that nobody has answered, a silence that breaks the group's usual pattern of near-constant replies.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the family group chat's recent activity?
options: The youngest cousin has stopped using the chat entirely.
The chat is exactly as active as it always has been.
Something may be different this week compared to their usual pattern.
Every message sent this week received an immediate reply.
quests.correctAnswer: Something may be different this week compared to their usual pattern.
quests.hint: Compare the described 'usual pattern of near-constant replies' with what has actually happened this week.
quests.explanation: A sharp drop from near-constant replies to unanswered questions suggests something out of the ordinary is affecting the family's usual communication pattern this week.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Bonus Structure That Favors the Top] The company's new incentive structure offers a modest 2 percent bonus pool for staff meeting standard targets, but a separate, uncapped bonus tier for the top 5 percent of performers, a structure the HR memo describes as 'rewarding excellence across the board.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about who benefits most from this new structure?
options: It distributes rewards equally regardless of individual performance.
It likely benefits a small group of top performers more than the wider staff.
It removes bonuses entirely for standard-target employees.
It benefits every employee to the exact same degree.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely benefits a small group of top performers more than the wider staff.
quests.hint: Compare the modest, capped pool for most staff with the uncapped tier reserved for a small top percentage.
quests.explanation: A modest, shared bonus pool contrasted with an uncapped tier for only the top 5 percent suggests the structure concentrates greater rewards among a small group, despite being described as benefiting 'everyone.'

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Waiting Room That Changed] The clinic replaces its outdated pamphlets and faded posters with a sleek new television displaying wellness tips, but longtime patients mention in an online review that average wait times, unaffected by the redecoration, have actually grown longer over the same period.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between the clinic's redecoration and its wait times?
options: The redecoration successfully reduced wait times.
Improving the waiting room's appearance did not address the underlying scheduling issue.
The redecoration directly caused wait times to increase.
Wait times and the waiting room's appearance are always directly connected.
quests.correctAnswer: Improving the waiting room's appearance did not address the underlying scheduling issue.
quests.hint: Think about what patients noticing longer waits, despite a nicer waiting room, suggests about what the redecoration actually fixed.
quests.explanation: Wait times growing longer despite a nicer waiting room suggests the redecoration addressed appearance rather than the underlying scheduling problem patients actually experience.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Festival Lineup Announced in Stages] The music festival releases its lineup in three separate waves over two months, each one revealing a few more names, a rollout strategy noticeably different from previous years when the full lineup was announced all at once months in advance.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the festival organizers' likely goal with this new approach?
options: They wanted to reveal less information than in previous years overall.
They were required to release the lineup this way by law.
They used the exact same strategy as every previous year.
They may be trying to generate sustained attention over a longer period.
quests.correctAnswer: They may be trying to generate sustained attention over a longer period.
quests.hint: Think about what spreading an announcement across three separate waves, rather than all at once, is designed to achieve over time.
quests.explanation: Releasing the lineup in three separate waves, unlike the single announcement in previous years, suggests a strategy aimed at keeping public attention and excitement building over a longer period.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Guidebook That Undersells a Detour] The printed guidebook lists the coastal detour as 'an optional scenic route, roughly twenty extra minutes,' but drivers who follow it report on travel forums that construction has extended the actual detour to nearly two hours, a discrepancy the guidebook's publisher has not yet corrected despite the book being reprinted twice since.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the guidebook's current accuracy on this point?
options: It has been fully updated to reflect the current construction.
It has not kept pace with a real change in road conditions.
The detour's time has actually decreased since the book was written.
No readers have ever reported an issue with this route.
quests.correctAnswer: It has not kept pace with a real change in road conditions.
quests.hint: Think about what being reprinted twice, yet still containing this outdated detail, suggests about whether it was corrected.
quests.explanation: The outdated detour time persisting through two reprints suggests the guidebook has not kept up with the actual change in road conditions.
